lane: lab H103 arm (a) (2026-10-25): "Did you know" mistake-fact hook at 0.0 s inside the proven Stop Saying "very X" container; 3 word beats with drawn pictures (same as control); kokoro am_michael 1.05, no music, 13-16 s. Variable = frame-0 hook only.

card.headline: Did you know there are better words than *"very tasty"*?

beats.speech: Did you know there are better words than very tasty? Here are three.
Delicious: Mia tries the soup. The soup is delicious.

card.headline: Mouth-watering
card.use: Next, a pie comes out of the oven.

beats.speech: Mouth-watering: Next, a pie comes out of the oven. It looks mouth-watering.
Scrumptious: Everyone wants more cake. The cake is scrumptious.
Which word will you use? Comment yours!

language_approval.notes: Hook was an overclaim ('very tasty sounds weak' - it is normal, correct English); now true: 'Did you know there are better words than very tasty? Here are three.' Beat 2: smell/looks mismatch fixed -> 'Next, a pie comes out of the oven. It looks mouth-watering.' (mouth-watering = looks/smells delicious before eating, nuance OK). Beat 3: tense shift fixed -> 'Everyone wants more cake. The cake is scrumptious.' Story chains soup -> pie -> cake in present tense. Speech == card text; caps OK; no policy issues.
